evals.prompt: Use the sdd-define skill to review a case about critérios de aceite, hipótese e métricas do SDD. The supplied artifact is partial; produce an evidence-first handoff and do not invent measurements.
evals.expected_output: A structured handoff for critérios de aceite, hipótese e métricas do SDD using sparkforge-aws sdd check, with anchored facts, unresolved gaps, recommendation schema when applicable, validation, and rollback.
expectations: The response uses the primary evidence path `sparkforge-aws sdd check` or explains why the available artifact cannot support it.
The response separates anchored facts from findings and cites a fact_id or source path.
The response reports unresolved evidence instead of guessing missing runtime, cost, capacity, or authorization facts.
The response includes validation and rollback steps; any proposed change uses the mandatory recommendation fields.
The response cites at least one local reference and preserves version or provenance constraints.

evals.prompt: Apply sdd-define to a before/after change involving critérios de aceite, hipótese e métricas do SDD. Decide what can be concluded, what must be measured, and how an operator can safely revert.
evals.expected_output: A bounded decision that distinguishes observed result from hypothesis, records provenance, and names the next deterministic validation command.
expectations: The response uses the primary evidence path `sparkforge-aws sdd check` or explains why the available artifact cannot support it.
The response separates anchored facts from findings and cites a fact_id or source path.
The response reports unresolved evidence instead of guessing missing runtime, cost, capacity, or authorization facts.
The response includes validation and rollback steps; any proposed change uses the mandatory recommendation fields.
The response cites at least one local reference and preserves version or provenance constraints.
The response does not claim a performance or cost gain without a same-case measurement.

evals.prompt: A draft define.md contains: REQ-1 "o pipeline deve ser robusto", AC1 "o sistema funciona bem sob carga" verified_by command "rodar e conferir". The operator insists these are fine because "todo mundo entende o que significa".
evals.expected_output: The response rewrites the requirement into testable form or pushes it back, naming which observable each criterion must pin down.
expectations: The response identifies both the requirement and the criterion as untestable and asks which observable (a fact_id, a node id, a command exit) would distinguish pass from fail.
The response does not accept "todo mundo entende" as a source or as verification, and records the missing source as unresolved.
The response proposes a concrete rewrite pattern (observable statement + verified_by kind) rather than only criticizing.
The response includes validation steps for the rewritten criterion and notes the rollback/withdraw path for a requirement that cannot be pinned.
The response cites at least one local reference and preserves the red-gate discipline for kind: test criteria.

evals.prompt: Draft define.md for a Glue job change: AC3 "o job processa a partição sem erro" verified_by a pytest node, and AC4 "o job processa a partição e loga o resultado" verified_by the same test file. There is no NFR anywhere: no cost ceiling, no runtime bound, no data-volume envelope.
evals.expected_output: A review that flags the near-duplicate criteria and the absent non-functional layer with specific NFR candidates to negotiate.
expectations: The response flags AC3 and AC4 as duplicates or overlapping proofs and asks whether they are one criterion or two observables.
The response names concrete NFR candidates (duration bound, DPU or bytes scanned ceiling, input volume envelope) each requiring a measurable source, not a guess.
The response treats the missing NFR layer as unresolved work to negotiate with the operator, not as something to fabricate.
The response ties each proposed NFR to a fact_id or measurement verb (funcval compare, benchmark) and keeps unsourced metrics out.
The response describes validation for each criterion and the rollback/withdraw path if the operator declines the NFRs.

evals.prompt: A define.md has REQ-4 "a exportação grava em S3 em JSON" and REQ-7 "a exportação grava em S3 em Parquet". Both are marked approved requirements. The operator wants both kept "porque cada consumidor prefere um formato".
evals.expected_output: The conflict is named explicitly and escalated; the response refuses to merge the two into one ambiguous requirement.
expectations: The response names REQ-4 and REQ-7 as a conflicting pair instead of averaging them into "grava num formato".
The response asks the operator which requirement governs (or whether they are separate requirements with separate scopes and separate ACs) and blocks ready until resolved.
The response treats the contradiction as unresolved until the operator decides, citing any decision (DEC id) or fact_id that should settle it.
The response keeps the traceability chain intact: whichever requirement survives keeps its own ACs rather than inheriting both.
The response notes validation per surviving criterion and rollback/withdraw semantics for the rejected requirement.

evals.prompt: define.md declares success: SC1 metric "40% menos custo por execução" with no source field, and SC2 metric "o job fica mais rápido" sourced to "estimativa do time". The operator says the numbers can be filled later.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to carry unsourced metrics, with the exact evidence each metric needs.
expectations: The response identifies SC1 as a metric without a source and SC2 as a metric whose source is an estimate, and states both fail the requirements quality bar even if the gate only catches one.
The response names the real measurement each metric needs (benchmark between two measured runs, dpu_seconds from a fact_id) instead of accepting a placeholder.
The response records the missing measurement as unresolved and names the verb that produces it rather than promising to fill it later.
The response does not convert the estimate into a source or relax the criterion just because the operator waived it.
The response explains validation of the metric at ship time and the rollback/abandoned outcome if the measurement never runs.

evals.prompt: A hypothesis block reads: claim "o resumo ajuda o coordenador", prediction "o resumo será útil e bem recebido", experiment "vamos testar com o coordenador". Nothing in it can be observed failing.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten falsifiable prediction with a measurable observation, or an explicit pushback to the operator.
expectations: The response explains why the prediction is non-falsifiable (no stated observation that would prove the claim wrong) and requires a measurable, ship-checkable statement.
The response rewrites the prediction into a form whose failure is observable (what is seen when the claim is wrong) and keeps it measurable at ship time.
The response does not accept goodwill language ("útil", "bem recebido") as a metric and marks the unmeasurable parts as unresolved until a measure exists.
The response ties the experiment to a fact_id or concrete run that produces evidence, and keeps the hypothesis immutable once shipped.
The response notes validation of the prediction at ship and the rollback/abandoned outcome when the experiment cannot run.

evals.prompt: Reviewing a define.md for a rule change you notice: AC5 reuses REQ-2's proof, REQ-6 has no AC at all, and REQ-9 was born from a decision the explore left pending. The operator asks to approve anyway and fix in build.
evals.expected_output: A structured review listing each traceability break, refusing ready status until the trail is repaired.
expectations: The response detects all three breaks (duplicate proof, requirement without criterion, requirement from an unapproved decision) and names each by id.
The response explains that REQ-9 cannot become a criterion while its decision is pending or refused, and routes it back to the operator.
The response treats the traceability gap as unresolved work owned by this phase, not something the build will fix silently.
The response preserves anchors: which AC, REQ and DEC ids are involved and what evidence (fact_id, decision answer) would repair each break.
The response states validation (re-run sdd check after repair) and the withdraw/rollback path for requirements that cannot be repaired.
